import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ulam's packing conjecture

Ulam's packing conjecture concerns the identity of the worst-packing convex solid in
three-dimensional Euclidean space. It says that the optimal density for packing congruent copies
of a ball is smaller than that for any other convex body: the ball is the convex solid which
forces the largest fraction of space to remain empty in its optimal packing. By Hales's proof of
the Kepler conjecture, $\delta(B^3) = \pi / \sqrt{18} \approx 0.7405$, so the conjecture says that
no convex solid forces more than $\approx 25.95\%$ of space to remain empty.

We follow the definitions of [Ka15, §1]. A *convex body* is a compact convex subset of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior. A set $\Xi$ of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is *admissible*
for $K$ (produces a *packing* of $K$) if the interiors of $\xi(K)$ and $\xi'(K)$ are disjoint for
all distinct $\xi, \xi' \in \Xi$. The *(upper) density* of the packing $\{\xi(K) : \xi \in \Xi\}$
is the fraction of space it fills,
$$\limsup_{r \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{vol}\big(\bigcup_{\xi \in \Xi} \xi(K) \cap
  B(0, r)\big)}{\operatorname{vol}(B(0, r))},$$
and the *packing density* $\delta(K)$ is the supremum of the densities of all packings of $K$.

The main statement `ulams_packing_conjecture` is the non-strict form "the ball is a global minimum
of $\delta$" used in [Ka14] and [Ka15]. The strict form "the ball packs strictly worse than every
other convex body", which is how the Wikipedia article phrases the conjecture, is
`ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.strict`. Isometries include reflections; the variant
`ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.rigid_motions` only allows orientation-preserving isometries
(rotations and translations), as for physically identical solids.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ulam's packing conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulam%27s_packing_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ga95] Gardner, M., *New Mathematical Diversions* (revised edition), MAA, 1995, postscript to
  the chapter "Packing Spheres".
- [Ka14] Kallus, Y., *The 3-ball is a local pessimum for packing*, Adv. Math. 264 (2014),
  355–370. [arXiv:1212.2551](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2551)
- [Ka15] Kallus, Y., *Pessimal packing shapes*, Geom. Topol. 19 (2015), 343–363.
  [arXiv:1305.0289](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0289)
- [Ha05] Hales, T. C., *A proof of the Kepler conjecture*, Ann. of Math. 162 (2005), 1065–1185.
-/

blocks.code:
def IsPacking (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  Ξ.PairwiseDisjoint fun ξ => interior (ξ '' K)
blocks.docstring:
A set `Ξ` of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is *admissible* for a set `K`, i.e. produces a
**packing** of `K`, if the congruent copies $\xi(K)$, $\xi \in \Xi$, have pairwise disjoint
interiors. Touching copies are allowed, as is standard for packings (see [Ka15, §1]).

justification.closest_existing_considered: SquarePacking.Packing (finite packing of n copies inside a container, FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean) and Mathoverflow34145 Configuration.IsPacking (rectangles in a unit square); Mathlib has no packing notion. Neither handles infinite packings of all of ℝ³.
justification.name: UlamsPackingConjecture.IsPacking
justification.why_needed: Need the notion 'a set Ξ of isometries of ℝ³ produces a packing of K' (copies ξ '' K have pairwise disjoint interiors). Defined as `Ξ.PairwiseDisjoint fun ξ => interior (ξ '' K)`.

blocks.name: IsPacking
blocks.text:
/-- A set `Ξ` of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is *admissible* for a set `K`, i.e. produces a
**packing** of `K`, if the congruent copies $\xi(K)$, $\xi \in \Xi$, have pairwise disjoint
interiors. Touching copies are allowed, as is standard for packings (see [Ka15, §1]). -/
def IsPacking (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  Ξ.PairwiseDisjoint fun ξ => interior (ξ '' K)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def upperDensity (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ =>
    volume ((⋃ ξ ∈ Ξ, ξ '' K) ∩ Metric.ball 0 r) / volume (Metric.ball (0 : ℝ³) r)) atTop
blocks.docstring:
The **(upper) density** of the family of congruent copies $\{\xi(K) : \xi \in \Xi\}$ of `K`:
the `limsup`, as $r \to \infty$, of the fraction of the ball of radius $r$ about the origin that
is covered by the union $\bigcup_{\xi \in \Xi} \xi(K)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.upperDensity for subsets of ℕ (FormalConjecturesForMathlib); nothing for volume density of subsets of Euclidean space in Mathlib.
justification.name: UlamsPackingConjecture.upperDensity
justification.why_needed: The upper density of a packing: limsup as r → ∞ of vol((⋃ ξ∈Ξ, ξ '' K) ∩ ball 0 r) / vol(ball 0 r) in ℝ≥0∞.

blocks.name: upperDensity
blocks.text:
/-- The **(upper) density** of the family of congruent copies $\{\xi(K) : \xi \in \Xi\}$ of `K`:
the `limsup`, as $r \to \infty$, of the fraction of the ball of radius $r$ about the origin that
is covered by the union $\bigcup_{\xi \in \Xi} \xi(K)$. -/
noncomputable def upperDensity (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ =>
    volume ((⋃ ξ ∈ Ξ, ξ '' K) ∩ Metric.ball 0 r) / volume (Metric.ball (0 : ℝ³) r)) atTop

blocks.code:
noncomputable def packingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ), upperDensity K Ξ
blocks.docstring:
The **packing density** $\delta(K)$ of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the supremum of the upper
densities of all packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of `K`, where the copies may be
moved by arbitrary isometries (see [Ka15, §1]).

justification.closest_existing_considered: No packing-density definition exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grepped for packingDensity, IsPacking, Kepler, limsup with volume).
justification.name: UlamsPackingConjecture.packingDensity
justification.why_needed: The packing density δ(K) = supremum of upperDensity K Ξ over all Ξ with IsPacking K Ξ; this is the quantity the conjecture compares between K and the ball.

blocks.name: packingDensity
blocks.text:
/-- The **packing density** $\delta(K)$ of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the supremum of the upper
densities of all packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of `K`, where the copies may be
moved by arbitrary isometries (see [Ka15, §1]). -/
noncomputable def packingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ), upperDensity K Ξ

blocks.code:
def IsRigidMotion (ξ : ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  0 < LinearMap.det (ξ.toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.linear : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³)
blocks.docstring:
An isometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *rigid motion* (an orientation-preserving isometry, i.e. a
rotation followed by a translation) if the determinant of its linear part is positive.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsometryEquiv.toRealAffineIsometryEquiv, LinearMap.det; Mathlib has no predicate for proper Euclidean motions.
justification.name: UlamsPackingConjecture.IsRigidMotion
justification.why_needed: Needed only for the rigid-motions variant: distinguishes orientation-preserving isometries (rotations+translations) from reflections via the sign of the determinant of the linear part (Mazur–Ulam).

blocks.name: IsRigidMotion
blocks.text:
/-- An isometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *rigid motion* (an orientation-preserving isometry, i.e. a
rotation followed by a translation) if the determinant of its linear part is positive. -/
def IsRigidMotion (ξ : ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  0 < LinearMap.det (ξ.toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.linear : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def rigidPackingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ ∧ ∀ ξ ∈ Ξ, IsRigidMotion ξ), upperDensity K Ξ
blocks.docstring:
The packing density of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$ when only packings by rigid motions
(rotations and translations, but no reflections) of `K` are allowed.

justification.name: UlamsPackingConjecture.rigidPackingDensity
justification.why_needed: Packing density restricted to packings by rigid motions, for the variant reading in which reflections are not allowed.

blocks.name: rigidPackingDensity
blocks.text:
/-- The packing density of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$ when only packings by rigid motions
(rotations and translations, but no reflections) of `K` are allowed. -/
noncomputable def rigidPackingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ ∧ ∀ ξ ∈ Ξ, IsRigidMotion ξ), upperDensity K Ξ

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isRigidMotion_refl : IsRigidMotion (IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³) := by
  have : ((IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³).toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.linear : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³) =
      LinearMap.id := by
    refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
    have := (IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³).toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquiv.toAffineMap
      |>.linearMap_vsub x 0
    simpa [IsometryEquiv.refl] using this
  rw [IsRigidMotion, this, LinearMap.det_id]
  exact zero_lt_one
blocks.docstring: The identity is a rigid motion.

theorem upperDensity_le_one (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : upperDensity K Ξ ≤ 1 := by
  refine limsup_le_of_le ?_ (Eventually.of_forall fun r => ?_)

  · refine ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul ?_

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem ulams_packing_conjecture (K : ConvexBody ℝ³) (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty) :
    packingDensity (Metric.closedBall 0 1) ≤ packingDensity K := by

blocks.docstring:
**Ulam's packing conjecture.** The ball is the worst-packing convex solid: for every
convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior), the optimal
density of packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of $K$ is at least the optimal density
of packings by congruent balls, $\delta(K) \ge \delta(B^3)$. That is, the ball is a global
minimum of the packing density $\delta$ over all three-dimensional convex bodies [Ka15, §1].

The requirement that $K$ has nonempty interior excludes degenerate (lower-dimensional) bodies,
which have packing density $0$.

optimal density for packing congruent balls is *smaller* than that for any other convex body,
i.e. $\delta(B^3) < \delta(K)$ for every convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ that is not itself
a ball.

claims.decomposer_note: Prop: for every convex body K ⊂ ℝ³ (compact convex with nonempty interior), the optimal packing density of congruent copies (translations and rotations allowed) of K is at least that of the unit ball, i.e. δ(K) ≥ δ(B³) = π/(3√2) by Hales's Kepler theorem; the article's phrasing 'smaller than that for any other convex body' suggests a strict inequality for non-balls, but Kallus's formulation ('ball is a global minimum of δ') is the non-strict form, so the strict/non-strict choice (and the upper-density definition of packing density as a sup over packings) must be fixed in the formalization.
claims.reviewer_why: c06's core is a faithful rendering of the decomposition Prop and of Kallus's definitions: convex body = `ConvexBody ℝ³` (compact, convex, nonempty) plus explicit `(interior K).Nonempty`; congruent copies = images under isometries `ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³` of genuine Euclidean space (`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`), which by Mazur–Ulam are all Euclidean congruences; packing = pairwise disjoint interiors (touching allowed); density of a packing = limsup_{r→∞} vol(⋃ξ(K) ∩ B(0,r))/vol(B(0,r)) in ℝ≥0∞ (Hales's/standard upper density; agrees with Kallus's count-based form for bounded bodies of positive volume); δ(K) = sup over packings; statement δ(B³) ≤ δ(K) (non-strict, Kallus's 'global minimum'). Edits: (1) dropped c06's `formal_proof using other_system` on the Kepler value, since Flyspeck does not prove this exact statement about the bespoke definition (c07's approach: cite Flyspeck in the docstring); (2) added c02's orientation-preserving (rigid-motion) variant, adapted to 3D/ℝ≥0∞, to cover the 'identical solids' reading in which reflections are disallowed, plus the API lemma rigidPackingDensity ≤ packingDensity and c02's test lemmas; (3) kept the strict Wikipedia-phrasing variant (K not a closed ball ⇒ δ(B³) < δ(K)), present identically in c02/c06/c07, as `variants.strict`.

context: Ulam's packing conjecture, named for Stanisław Ulam, is a conjecture about the highest possible packing density of identical convex solids in three-dimensional Euclidean space. The conjecture says that the optimal density for packing congruent spheres is smaller than that for any other convex body. That is, according to the conjecture, the ball is the convex solid which forces the largest fraction of space to remain empty in its optimal packing structure. This conjecture is therefore related to the Kepler conjecture about sphere packing. Since the solution to the Kepler conjecture establishes that identical balls must leave ≈25.95% of the space empty, Ulam's conjecture is equivalent to the statement that no other convex solid forces that much space to be left empty.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ulam's packing conjecture

Ulam's packing conjecture concerns the identity of the worst-packing convex solid in
three-dimensional Euclidean space. It says that the optimal density for packing congruent copies
of a ball is smaller than that for any other convex body: the ball is the convex solid which
forces the largest fraction of space to remain empty in its optimal packing. By Hales's proof of
the Kepler conjecture, $\delta(B^3) = \pi / \sqrt{18} \approx 0.7405$, so the conjecture says that
no convex solid forces more than $\approx 25.95\%$ of space to remain empty.

We follow the definitions of [Ka15, §1]. A *convex body* is a compact convex subset of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior. A set $\Xi$ of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is *admissible*
for $K$ (produces a *packing* of $K$) if the interiors of $\xi(K)$ and $\xi'(K)$ are disjoint for
all distinct $\xi, \xi' \in \Xi$. The *(upper) density* of the packing $\{\xi(K) : \xi \in \Xi\}$
is the fraction of space it fills,
$$\limsup_{r \to \infty} \frac{\operatorname{vol}\big(\bigcup_{\xi \in \Xi} \xi(K) \cap
  B(0, r)\big)}{\operatorname{vol}(B(0, r))},$$
and the *packing density* $\delta(K)$ is the supremum of the densities of all packings of $K$.

The main statement `ulams_packing_conjecture` is the non-strict form "the ball is a global minimum
of $\delta$" used in [Ka14] and [Ka15]. The strict form "the ball packs strictly worse than every
other convex body", which is how the Wikipedia article phrases the conjecture, is
`ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.strict`. Isometries include reflections; the variant
`ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.rigid_motions` only allows orientation-preserving isometries
(rotations and translations), as for physically identical solids.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ulam's packing conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulam%27s_packing_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ga95] Gardner, M., *New Mathematical Diversions* (revised edition), MAA, 1995, postscript to
  the chapter "Packing Spheres".
- [Ka14] Kallus, Y., *The 3-ball is a local pessimum for packing*, Adv. Math. 264 (2014),
  355–370. [arXiv:1212.2551](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2551)
- [Ka15] Kallus, Y., *Pessimal packing shapes*, Geom. Topol. 19 (2015), 343–363.
  [arXiv:1305.0289](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0289)
- [Ha05] Hales, T. C., *A proof of the Kepler conjecture*, Ann. of Math. 162 (2005), 1065–1185.
-/

open MeasureTheory Filter
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal Real

namespace UlamsPackingConjecture

/-- A set `Ξ` of isometries of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is *admissible* for a set `K`, i.e. produces a
**packing** of `K`, if the congruent copies $\xi(K)$, $\xi \in \Xi$, have pairwise disjoint
interiors. Touching copies are allowed, as is standard for packings (see [Ka15, §1]). -/
def IsPacking (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  Ξ.PairwiseDisjoint fun ξ => interior (ξ '' K)

/-- The **(upper) density** of the family of congruent copies $\{\xi(K) : \xi \in \Xi\}$ of `K`:
the `limsup`, as $r \to \infty$, of the fraction of the ball of radius $r$ about the origin that
is covered by the union $\bigcup_{\xi \in \Xi} \xi(K)$. -/
noncomputable def upperDensity (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  limsup (fun r : ℝ =>
    volume ((⋃ ξ ∈ Ξ, ξ '' K) ∩ Metric.ball 0 r) / volume (Metric.ball (0 : ℝ³) r)) atTop

/-- The **packing density** $\delta(K)$ of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the supremum of the upper
densities of all packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of `K`, where the copies may be
moved by arbitrary isometries (see [Ka15, §1]). -/
noncomputable def packingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ), upperDensity K Ξ

/-- An isometry of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *rigid motion* (an orientation-preserving isometry, i.e. a
rotation followed by a translation) if the determinant of its linear part is positive. -/
def IsRigidMotion (ξ : ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  0 < LinearMap.det (ξ.toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.linear : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³)

/-- The packing density of a set `K` in $\mathbb{R}^3$ when only packings by rigid motions
(rotations and translations, but no reflections) of `K` are allowed. -/
noncomputable def rigidPackingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨆ (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) (_ : IsPacking K Ξ ∧ ∀ ξ ∈ Ξ, IsRigidMotion ξ), upperDensity K Ξ

/-- A single copy of `K` is a packing. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_singleton (K : Set ℝ³) : IsPacking K {IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³} :=
  Set.pairwiseDisjoint_singleton _ _

/-- A set of isometries producing pairwise disjoint copies of `K` is admissible for `K`. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isPacking_of_pairwise_disjoint (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³))
    (h : Ξ.Pairwise fun ξ ξ' => Disjoint (ξ '' K) (ξ' '' K)) : IsPacking K Ξ :=
  h.imp fun _ _ hd => hd.mono interior_subset interior_subset

/-- The identity is a rigid motion. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isRigidMotion_refl : IsRigidMotion (IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³) := by
  have : ((IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³).toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.linear : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³) =
      LinearMap.id := by
    refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
    have := (IsometryEquiv.refl ℝ³).toRealAffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquiv.toAffineMap
      |>.linearMap_vsub x 0
    simpa [IsometryEquiv.refl] using this
  rw [IsRigidMotion, this, LinearMap.det_id]
  exact zero_lt_one

/-- Every family of congruent copies of `K` has upper density at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem upperDensity_le_one (K : Set ℝ³) (Ξ : Set (ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³)) : upperDensity K Ξ ≤ 1 := by
  refine limsup_le_of_le ?_ (Eventually.of_forall fun r => ?_)
  · exact isCoboundedUnder_le_of_le atTop fun _ => zero_le _
  · refine ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul ?_
    rw [one_mul]
    exact measure_mono Set.inter_subset_right

/-- The packing density of any set is at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem packingDensity_le_one (K : Set ℝ³) : packingDensity K ≤ 1 :=
  iSup₂_le fun Ξ _ => upperDensity_le_one K Ξ

/-- Restricting to rigid motions can only decrease the packing density. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem rigidPackingDensity_le_packingDensity (K : Set ℝ³) :
    rigidPackingDensity K ≤ packingDensity K :=
  iSup₂_le fun Ξ h => le_iSup₂ (f := fun Ξ (_ : IsPacking K Ξ) => upperDensity K Ξ) Ξ h.1

/-- **Ulam's packing conjecture.** The ball is the worst-packing convex solid: for every
convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior), the optimal
density of packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by congruent copies of $K$ is at least the optimal density
of packings by congruent balls, $\delta(K) \ge \delta(B^3)$. That is, the ball is a global
minimum of the packing density $\delta$ over all three-dimensional convex bodies [Ka15, §1].

The requirement that $K$ has nonempty interior excludes degenerate (lower-dimensional) bodies,
which have packing density $0$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem ulams_packing_conjecture (K : ConvexBody ℝ³) (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty) :
    packingDensity (Metric.closedBall 0 1) ≤ packingDensity K := by
  sorry

/-- The strict form of **Ulam's packing conjecture**, as phrased in the Wikipedia article: the
optimal density for packing congruent balls is *smaller* than that for any other convex body,
i.e. $\delta(B^3) < \delta(K)$ for every convex body $K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ that is not itself
a ball. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.strict (K : ConvexBody ℝ³)
    (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty)
    (hK' : ∀ (c : ℝ³) (r : ℝ), (K : Set ℝ³) ≠ Metric.closedBall c r) :
    packingDensity (Metric.closedBall 0 1) < packingDensity K := by
  sorry

/-- **Ulam's packing conjecture** for packings by rigid motions, i.e. for "identical convex
solids" [Ga95] that may be rotated and translated but not reflected: for every convex body
$K \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, the optimal density of packings of $\mathbb{R}^3$ by rigid-motion copies
of $K$ is at least the optimal density of packings by congruent balls. Since rigid-motion packings
are packings, this implies `ulams_packing_conjecture`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.rigid_motions (K : ConvexBody ℝ³)
    (hK : (interior (K : Set ℝ³)).Nonempty) :
    rigidPackingDensity (Metric.closedBall 0 1) ≤ rigidPackingDensity K := by
  sorry

/-- **The Kepler conjecture** (Hales [Ha05]; formally verified in HOL Light and Isabelle by the
[Flyspeck project](https://github.com/flyspeck/flyspeck)): the optimal packing density of congruent
balls in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\pi / \sqrt{18} = \pi / (3\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.7405$, so balls must
leave $\approx 25.95\%$ of space empty. Hence Ulam's packing conjecture says that no convex solid
forces more than $\approx 25.95\%$ of space to remain empty. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem packingDensity_closedBall :
    packingDensity (Metric.closedBall 0 1) = ENNReal.ofReal (π / √18) := by
  sorry

end UlamsPackingConjecture

items: Non-strict vs strict: the main declaration `ulams_packing_conjecture` uses the non-strict form δ(B³) ≤ δ(K) for every convex body K (Kallus 2014/2015: 'the ball is a global minimum of δ'; this is also the operative formula δ(K) ≥ δ(B³) in the decomposition notes). The Wikipedia article's strict wording ('smaller than that for any other convex body') is recorded as a separate declaration `ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.strict`: δ(B³) < δ(K) for every convex body K that is not a closed ball (of any centre and radius).

Convex body = Mathlib `ConvexBody ℝ³` (convex, compact, nonempty) together with the hypothesis `(interior K).Nonempty`, matching Kallus's definition. Mathlib's ConvexBody alone does not require nonempty interior; without that hypothesis lower-dimensional bodies (density 0) would falsify the statement.

Congruent copies are images under arbitrary isometries `ℝ³ ≃ᵢ ℝ³` (Mathlib IsometryEquiv), which includes reflections, following Kallus's definition ('a set of isometries Ξ is admissible for K'). Restricting to proper rigid motions (SO(3) ⋉ ℝ³) would give a possibly larger packing density for chiral bodies and hence a formally stronger conjecture; this reading was not chosen.
A packing requires only pairwise disjoint *interiors* of the copies (touching allowed), as is standard and as in Kallus; this makes the densest sphere packings genuine packings.

Packing density is defined via the upper (limsup) volume density in balls centred at the origin, i.e. δ(K) = sup over packings of limsup_{r→∞} vol(⋃ξ(K) ∩ B(0,r))/vol(B(0,r)), valued in ℝ≥0∞. Kallus instead uses a counting-based lower mean volume d(Ξ) = liminf (4πr³/3)/#{ξ : ‖ξ(0)‖ < r} and δ = sup vol(K)/d(Ξ); the two agree for bounded bodies with nonempty interior. Values are in ℝ≥0∞ (division by vol(B(0,r)) is well defined for r > 0; for r ≤ 0 the term is 0/0 = 0 which is irrelevant at atTop).
The reference ball is `Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ³) 1`; packing density is invariant under isometries and dilations so the choice of centre/radius is immaterial.

Extra declarations beyond the slot: API lemmas `upperDensity_le_one`, `packingDensity_le_one` (proved), a test `isPacking_singleton` (proved), and `packingDensity_closedBall : packingDensity (closedBall 0 1) = ENNReal.ofReal (π / √18)` tagged `research solved` (Kepler conjecture, Hales; Flyspeck formal proof linked via `formal_proof using other_system`). These test the definitions and connect to the article's remark that balls leave ≈25.95% of space empty.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities and how they were resolved: (a) Strict vs non-strict. Wikipedia's article says 'smaller than that for any other convex body' (strict); Kallus (the primary literature) says 'the ball is a global minimum of δ' (non-strict); the decomposition Prop is non-strict. Main declaration is non-strict; strict form is `ulams_packing_conjecture.variants.strict` with hypothesis `∀ c r, K ≠ closedBall c r` (with nonempty interior in force this excludes exactly the genuine balls; checked that closedBall c r with r ≤ 0 has empty interior). (b) Reflections. Standard δ(K) and Kallus use all isometries; Gardner's 'identical convex solids' could mean proper motions only. Main uses all isometries (the weaker claim); `variants.rigid_motions` restricts to det>0 isometries on both sides. (c) Comparison against δ(closedBall 0 1) rather than the numeric π/√18, so the open conjecture does not bake in Hales's theorem; the Kepler value δ(B³) = π/√18 is stated separately as `research solved` (with sorry, no formal_proof attribute, Flyspeck cited in docstring), matching the article's '≈25.95% empty' remark and testing the definitions. Candidate verdicts: c01 REJECTED — uses `Fin 3 → ℝ` (sup metric): its isometries are only signed permutations + translations and its balls are cubes, so it is not the Euclidean congruent-copy packing density. c03/c08 correct but conjoin the solved Kepler equality into the open theorem (less clean). c04 correct-in-substance count-based density with ncard (finite for nonempty-interior bodies) but non-standard, compares to the constant only. c05 makes the strict form the main slot, contrary to the decomposition Prop. c02/c06/c07 all faithful; c06 chosen as base (3D-specific, IsometryEquiv idiom matching Wikipedia/SquarePacking.lean), with c02's rigid-motion variant merged and c06's Flyspeck `formal_proof` attribute removed as an overclaim. All candidates compiled; final file compiles with only the 4 expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. Definitions are kept in the problem file (single-output constraint); a maintainer may prefer moving the general definitions to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
